name: Proximate-generation interconnection
desc: How co-located or nearby load-plus-generation (hybrid) facilities are studied and interconnected together.

letters.desc: Geographic and electrical proximity between a large load and its associated supply resource is the key condition justifying joint study. The filer endorses SPP's HILLGA definition of no more than two substations away as a useful starting point, while allowing regional calibration.
quotes: To the extent that a new large load and new generation or storage resource are geographically and electrically proximate, studying them together would reduce network upgrades, lower costs, and reduce the need for critical supply chain components.

letters.desc: The Alliance supports a requirement that transmission providers assess reliability, resilience, and service quality impacts on Tribal communities before undertaking major system modifications for large-load integration. It also calls for delegated Consultation with Tribal governments where large-load integration may affect service on or near Tribal lands.
quotes: The Commission should make clear that transmission providers may not shift operational risks, reliability degradation, or the costs of new load integration onto existing customers - particularly those in Tribal and disadvantaged communities.

The Alliance urges the Commission to require transmission providers to include an analysis of potential reliability, resilience, and service quality impacts on Tribal communities as part of their transmission service planning for large loads.

letters.desc: ACC emphasizes that co-located resources should be permitted at all viable proximity levels to ensure no solutions are excluded and developers can deploy resources as conditions allow.
quotes: Recognize the value of co-locating generation or storage both behind the meter and near or adjacent to the meter, to ensure no potential solutions are excluded.

letters.desc: Arevia supports giving large load interconnection customers the same build options available to generator customers.
quotes: Arevia would be open and supportive to this priority.

letters.desc: Base Power contends that siting rules should permit generation to support new loads regardless of distance from the load's point of interconnection, provided facilities are electrically proximal and performance is verifiable. The core principle is that dispatchability, not geography, defines reliability value.
quotes: New load-enabling generation siting constraints should allow for electrically proximal resources.

Siting for dispatchable capacity additions in service of new loads should remain open to both those behind the same and electrically proximal points of interconnection on the bulk transmission system, reflecting the functional reality that location does not diminish reliability value when performance is verifiable.

The defining feature of resource adequacy is dispatchability, not geography. A resource that can increase or decrease its output or load in response to an operator signal provides the same system benefit whether it is co-located with the facility it serves or operates under a contractual arrangement elsewhere.

Under the HILLGA process, supplemental generating facilities procured to serve such loads may be considered in a combined application with the load, expediting interconnection, when located electrically proximal, defined as no more than two bulk-system substations away from the load.

in the course of normal grid operations, it is far less expensive and far more reliable to meet incremental resource adequacy needs with supplemental generation, whether located on-site or electrical proximal, than to compensate a large load for curtailing

letters.desc: Large loads that commit to flexibility should be able to interconnect provisionally while transmission infrastructure for firm service is being built, enabling faster online operations. Transparent constraint identification from studies enables such arrangements.
quotes: Recognize that load flexibility (including hybrid configurations of load including generation or energy storage) may also allow a large load to interconnect provisionally while needed infrastructure is built for firm service to create a path for large loads to come online quickly but reliably in the interim.

Pacific Gas & Electric's ("PG&E") "Flex Connect" Program offers the Commission a useful model for the transparency they should require of Transmission Owners. In constrained areas of PG&E's grid, PG&E identifies the hours and amount that customers need to curtail (or otherwise provide flexibility from on-site energy generation or storage) if they wish to defer upgrades and interconnect immediately.

Customers should be allowed to use load flexibility (including hybrid configurations of load including generation or energy storage to enable flexibility) to interconnect provisionally to the system while needed infrastructure is being built to achieve a higher level of transmission service.

letters.desc: AI-SCA emphasizes connecting to transmission at existing sites with available power and developing new local supply quickly, framing proximity to existing power infrastructure as key to meeting national security and economic goals.
quotes: Approaches such as direct market access and new supply arrangements, such as co-location (or hybrid facilities), bring your own power, and behind-the-meter generation, can enable faster connection to the grid for large load customers like data centers, reshoring of manufacturing, and other industrial processes while ensuring that interconnecting customers are responsible for associated costs of network upgrades.

Timely interconnection to the transmission system via existing sites with power and opportunities to quickly develop new and additional power supplies is paramount to meeting national security and economic development goals.

letters.desc: Constellation argues that net-based transmission rates create strong incentives for large loads to locate near existing generation, reducing the need for network upgrades. Applying RMR/SSR requirements to co-locating existing generators undermines those co-location incentives.
quotes: Replacing PJM's Necessary Study process with RMR/SSR retirement studies that would impose broad new network costs on a class of existing resources for the simple act of serving a customer through a co-located configuration chosen by the customer, which may be the only option to serve the load in a timely fashion.

letters.desc: Constellation argues that connecting load at sites with existing, proven reliability paths is the most efficient use of the grid and that leaving such capacity idle while load waits is unjust.
quotes: It is unjust and unreasonable not to fully utilize existing infrastructure and proven reliability paths while new load waits for service.

letters.desc: FERC should not preempt or override state jurisdictions that are already successfully and expeditiously connecting large loads, as demonstrated by data-center investments in California, New York, Texas, Louisiana, and other regions.
quotes: Simply put, FERC should not preempt jurisdictions that are expeditiously connecting large loads.

letters.desc: Critical Loop encourages FERC to require or encourage transparent, hosting-capacity-style load data so customers can identify sites where on-site resources and flexible operation meaningfully reduce upgrade needs.
quotes: encouraging or requiring transparent, hosting-capacity-style data for load so that customers can see where flexible operation and on-site resources can meaningfully reduce upgrade needs and select sites accordingly.

letters.desc: Because onsite generation offsets withdrawal, hybrid facilities have a smaller footprint on the transmission grid than standalone large loads. Crusoe asks FERC to reflect this difference in study methodology and cost allocation.
quotes: Hybrid facility structures cause significantly less impact on the transmission grid than large loads that do not bring generation.  Thus, where hybrid facilities are proposed, the load and generation should be studied together to get an accurate picture of the load's impact on the grid.

letters.desc: Speed is essential to interconnecting large loads and connecting waiting generation capacity. CTC emphasizes that reconductoring with advanced conductors can double transmission capacity in 6 to 24 months by reusing towers and rights-of-way, which is necessary to unlock the 2.6 terawatts of generation currently in interconnection queues.
quotes: This speed-to-power approach is key when discussing steps that can and must be taken in order to add new large loads to the power system.
Reconductoring existing lines with advanced conductors can often double capacity in 6-24 months by reusing towers and rights-of-way, and avoiding many siting reviews.
This is critical to connecting existing generation to demand, as well as unleashing the 2.6 Terawatts of generation capacity currently sitting in interconnection queues.

letters.desc: EEI endorses using electrical proximity as a criterion for accelerated study benefits, consistent with the SPP approach that links load-limited generation resources to nearby high-impact large load customers.
quotes: the Commission should extend accelerated study benefits—if any are established in a Final Rule—to arrangements involving load and facilities located in proximity to each other but not at the same point of interconnection.

letters.desc: Eolian argues from engineering principles and direct experience that generation close to load requires less transmission infrastructure. Existing rules block integrated study of planned loads and nearby generation, causing duplicative upgrade requirements that harm both load and generation project viability.
quotes: Eolian has experienced multiple cases where a transmission provider's refusal to perform an integrated study of load and generation has caused duplicative upgrade requirements that could have been avoided if load and generation had been considered together, which has impacted the business viability of both load and generation.

letters.desc: Eolian endorses a technical de-minimis loop flow standard for defining electrical proximity of hybrid components, rather than rigid physical adjacency, to allow projects to navigate land, retail law, and commercial constraints while still qualifying for expedited interconnection.
quotes: We urge the Commission to set standards that allow for configurations to flexibly navigate commercial and local regulatory considerations while adhering to demonstrable de-minimis impacts on the transmission system and thereby qualifying for expedited interconnection.

letters.desc: Eolian argues that generators siting assets to open headroom for nearby load get no credit under current rules, removing the incentive to locate efficiently. It proposes a transmission capacity tag mechanism through which generators could monetize the headroom they create and loads could contract for it.
quotes: we have not encountered any transmission provider that currently has a process which (i) adequately integrates or coordinates the interconnection of supply resources and load, (ii) provides developers of supply resources such as Eolian with adequate incentive to locate generation and storage assets in a manner that opens additional system headroom for load interconnection, or (iii) offers the full range of transmission service options necessary to allow supply and load to coordinate to optimally use the existing system and reduce transmission infrastructure needs.

The Commission must require transmission providers to offer transmission services that match the ability of loads to use the capabilities of adjacent generation, including non-firm and reduced service options. Such service must allow the load to take service when the grid is unconstrained and the supply resource is not available (including when a battery resource is charging) while electing to curtail when the grid is constrained.

the Commission should explicitly direct transmission providers to make the non-firm services available to all loads willing and able to limit withdrawals from the transmission system rather than limiting availability only to co-located loads.

Under PJM's current rules, however, there is little incentive for developers such as Eolian to locate assets to provide these system benefits. Developers do not get any credit or earn any additional revenues for opening additional system capacity.

the generation interconnection process afforded generators the ability to generate 'tags' representing the transmission capacity that the proposed generation opens. Such a transmission capacity tag could then be used in the load interconnection process, allowing load to contract with generation to support development that enables development to move forward that is currently on hold.

letters.desc: Equinix proposes that large-load interconnection customers be allowed to aggregate nearby resources in sufficient proximity to resolve or mitigate constraints that would otherwise trigger upgrade costs. This approach would reduce costs and timelines without requiring on-site generation.
quotes: the vast majority of data centers, such as colocation and edge data centers, must be located as close to the businesses and public entities that they serve as possible.

Those data centers located in dense metropolitan areas should be able to tap into the wealth of flexibility opportunities that surround them, creating a mutual benefit for those commercial, industrial or even residential users that could receive enhanced energy equipment or could easily absorb curtailment at a much lower economic and performance cost.
large load interconnection customers should be allowed to include what could be termed 'aggregated resource' proposals in their interconnection requests.

Penalizing those large loads that, for national security, financial sector or other reasons must maintain extremely high up-time, and for those same reasons are geographically constrained to areas that have limited ability to incorporate backup or co-located generation, would be contrary to national interests.

letters.desc: esVolta asks FERC to adopt PJM's load deliverability area and MISO's local resource zone as the geographic proximity test for expedited study eligibility, rather than requiring strict co-location on site. Resources within the same zone that have load agreements should qualify.
quotes: Studying large loads together with BESS aligns closely with the Department's emphasis on the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads. Where a large load is electrically proximate to BESS that is designed to provide the services described above, the combined configuration is better able to satisfy applicable reliability and power quality criteria without imposing excessive incremental burdens on the transmission system.

esVolta encourages the Commission to consider a similar approach in any rulemaking it promulgates to address the integration of large loads and ensure that standalone BESS either located "in close proximity", "near by" the data center, or either electrically or co-located onsite with the data center or the large load is deemed an eligible supply resource to receive expedited interconnection study treatment along with the data center load.

esVolta would go even further to support approaches in PJM that rightfully identify supply resources in the same "load deliverability area or LDA" as an eligible resource for the expedited interconnection process and similarly, in MISO, standalone storage and other resources that have agreements with large loads to provide needed resources and are located in the same "local resource zone or LRZ" should be deemed eligible for an expedited interconnection process completed within 90 days.

letters.desc: Fervo supports cost responsibility frameworks that reflect actual local and systemic benefits from hybrids and allow existing projects to benefit from new rules without forced restudy when electing hybrid framework.
quotes: Fervo therefore encourages the Commission to ensure that cost responsibility is applied in a way that reflects actual system benefits and not over-assign costs to hybrids that reduce net flows or improve local reliability.

Allowing transmission providers to apply the new modeling assumptions, hybrid treatment rules, and coordinated study processes to existing queue positions, without forcing restudy or loss of queue priority, would ensure that early geothermal hybrid projects can access the benefits of reforms intended for exactly this type of configuration.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy argues that experienced transmission-owning utilities are better positioned than data center customers to design, permit, and build interconnection facilities, and that keeping construction with utilities is the fastest path to power.
quotes: the best way to achieve the ANOPR's goal of timely large load interconnections is to have experienced transmission-owning utilities design and build the transmission facilities needed to interconnect large load customers.

letters.desc: Fluence asks FERC to allow flexibility commitments to be met by resources adjacent to load, not requiring on-site generation, which aligns with a proximate resource principle.
quotes: The Commission should ensure that load commitments to flexibility can be met by resources physically and/or electrically adjacent to load.

letters.desc: FuelCell Energy supports giving load customers and hybrid projects the option to build when they are not the transmission owner, ensuring that hybrid facilities can move forward on timelines comparable to other resource types and are not disadvantaged by co-location.
quotes: A facility with a net 10 MW output could, in practice, consist of a 700 MW generator paired with a 690 MW load. Such cases demonstrate the need for a distinct process that enables Transmission Owners and Transmission Providers to properly assess the full system impacts of hybrid facilities
the Commission should ensure that the Transmission Owner or Transmission Provider study and account for the full amount of load and MWs of generation that make up a hybrid facility

load interconnection customer is not the Transmission Owner or Transmission Provider, the customer should be afforded the same or equivalent option to build as is currently available to generator interconnection customers

hybrid facilities should have the same right to exercise an option to build as traditional generation-only projects. Without such clarity, hybrid developers could face unnecessary uncertainty or delays, which would in turn discourage investment

letters.desc: Google strongly supports nationwide rules for expedited interconnection of large loads paired with electrically proximate generation, modeled on SPP's HILLGA framework. Study methodology should reflect actual injection and withdrawal rights, and financial commitments (such as PPAs) should be required to qualify for the expedited track.
quotes: The Commission should establish nationwide rules governing interconnection arrangements involving generation resources paired with new large loads that share either the same or an electrically proximate point of interconnection.

The coordinated and expedited study of electrically proximate large loads and grid-connected generators will facilitate the development of digital infrastructure while minimizing the strain on, and maximizing the use of, existing power infrastructure.

The Commission should craft procedures to expedite the transmission-level interconnection of new load and electrically proximate generation where a large load developer makes a financial commitment, via a power purchase agreement ('PPA') or a similar agreement, to bring online a new generating facility, uprate or expand an existing generating facility, retain a generating facility that would otherwise retire, or enable a resource that would otherwise be uneconomic to undergo fuel-switching.

To ensure that the generation is appropriately tailored to the new load, those commitments should match the load's ramp and utilization schedule on a one-for-one basis with accredited generation, verified load flexibility, or demand response capabilities.
Paired, electrically proximate load and generation should be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights that they request.

letters.desc: Google endorses an optional, time-limited expedited study path for generation electrically proximate to a new large load, modeled on SPP's HILLGA proposal. The pathway must be technology neutral, open to storage, and must not block loads that cannot find a proximate generator.
quotes: Google agrees with commenters that the Commission should establish pathways for facilitating the expedited study and interconnection of electrically proximate pairs of generation and load, as doing so will reduce the network upgrades needed to interconnect new resources, which can accelerate the pace at which new generation comes online.

the Commission should ensure that any such regime: Provides an optional pathway (i.e., an incentive) and not a requirement that effectively blocks the interconnection of large loads that, for whatever reason, are not or cannot be paired with electrically proximate generation.

Ensures that any expedited interconnection process is technology neutral. In particular, it must be open to storage resources, which can deploy more rapidly than any other grid resource and can manage the impact of large loads on the grid.

letters.org: Governor Josh Shapiro and Governor Glenn Youngkin
letters.desc: The governors support requiring LLAs to invest in nearby energy generation and storage as part of the interconnection framework, mirroring the bipartisan PJM governors' proposal.
quotes: this framework would provide strong incentives for LLAs to invest in nearby new energy generation and storage resources, to curtail during tight market conditions, and to take responsibility for their network upgrade costs.

letters.desc: GridCARE emphasizes that unlocking latent capacity on existing infrastructure can serve near-term large-load demand while long-lead transmission projects are still under development, complementing rather than replacing new investment.
quotes: A framework that better utilizes existing assets can serve near-term load, maintain affordability, and support the investment environment for utilities while long-lead projects progress through permitting and construction.

letters.desc: Helion highlights that fusion energy is independent of geographic constraints, fuel supply chains, and weather conditions, enabling siting at load centers. This flexibility allows generation to be deployed precisely where needed without the limitations of traditional baseload sources.
quotes: Helion's independence from geographic constraints, continuous fuel supply chains, and weather conditions enables siting directly alongside data centers, manufacturing facilities, and other large users.

letters.desc: The IL OAG urges that paired generation be sited within the same market area as the large load, even if not at the same point of interconnection, to keep transmission system costs low and avoid drawing on distant resources already serving the existing customer base.
quotes: The ANOPR should expressly include discussion of requiring large load to be matched with equivalent new generation in order to connect to the federal transmission system.

New load and generation may be sited at the same point of interconnection (i.e. hybrid facilities), but to minimize costs on the transmission system they should be sited within the smallest applicable market area even if they are not at the same point of interconnection.

letters.desc: Kiesling argues that poor cost allocation drives flexible loads into private microgrids, undermining reliability. Marginal-cost-aligned tariffs are necessary to keep grid-supportive large loads interconnected rather than isolated.
quotes: Aligning cost allocation with marginal impacts ensures that flexible loads remain part of the bulk system rather than retreating into private microgrids.

letters.desc: When a large load sites near a generator to reduce network upgrade costs, credible commercial arrangements and aligned in-service dates should be required to prevent queue piggybacking.
quotes: If a large load sites near a generator solely to reduce network upgrades, require demonstration of credible commercial arrangements and aligned in‑service dates (to avoid que piggybacking).

letters.desc: The filer argues that only VPP resources electrically proximate to the constrained node can provide genuine interconnection relief, consistent with AC power flow physics. Dispersed residential portfolios across a multi-state RTO footprint cannot relieve a specific substation constraint.
quotes: Residential VPP resources are necessarily dispersed across residential neighborhoods throughout a utility service territory or RTO region. In PJM, a Demand Response aggregator might enroll 50,000 smart thermostats distributed across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, and Delaware. These devices provide regional load reduction, but they are not concentrated at the specific transmission node serving the data center.
Load reduction at Location A only relieves constraints at Location B if A and B are electrically proximate in the network topology.

such contributions must be demonstrated through the same rigorous interconnection study methodology applied to all other resources: Locational specificity... Temporal certainty... Operational firmness... Verification and measurement

letters.desc: Hopkins urges FERC to take action before the Shapiro price cap protecting Pennsylvania ratepayers expires in 2030, warning that costs will rise further without reform.
quotes: act before the Shapiro price cap expires in 2030. The cap has provided temporary protection for Pennsylvania ratepayers. Without action, costs will increase even more.

letters.desc: The filer argues that data center siting should be directed toward nodes with demonstrated fault-level capacity, which in practice means legacy heavy industrial sites in the Rust Belt corridor. Stiff-point and demand cap standards convert grid physics into market signals, favoring geographies where the foundational engineering already exists rather than locations that impose cascading costs on the system.
quotes: Extending the fault-level qualification standards that utilities applied to electric arc furnace operators beginning in the 1970s to data center interconnection, combined with node-level demand caps embedded in interconnection agreements, would implement a stiff-point siting standard that directs large digital infrastructure loads toward the transmission nodes capable of absorbing them without cascading grid stress or ratepayer cost socialization.

The requirement that large-load interconnection applicants demonstrate node adequacy, or fund the specific localized upgrades required to achieve it, places network optimization costs on the party whose siting decision creates them.

Legacy Rust Belt industrial districts carry precisely the grid characteristics that the stiff-point framework rewards. The industrial districts that supported heavy manufacturing, integrated steel production, and automotive assembly during the postwar decades required, and received, high-capacity transmission lines and substations engineered to absorb the kind of volatile, nonlinear loads that are exceptionally difficult to manage on a regional network.

RTOs and ISOs should establish a priority processing track for large-load interconnection applications at nodes with demonstrated stiff-point characteristics. Legacy heavy industrial sites in the Rust Belt corridor that carried industrial loads of comparable or greater magnitude within the past thirty years should be eligible for expedited preliminary qualification based on documented interconnection history.

letters.desc: IFP broadly endorses the combined framework of Principles 3, 5, 7, 8, and 9 as a viable path to deploying gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure while preserving grid reliability.
quotes: IFP strongly supports the Principles identified in the Commission's ANOPR.

letters.desc: IECA argues that a load contractually tied to generation at a physically proximate point of interconnection should be treated the same as a behind-the-meter co-location arrangement. It supports joint study and expedited approval for both single-point and proximate-point configurations.
quotes: a large load which interconnects with the grid at one point of interconnection and is contractually tied to one or more comparably-sized generation resources which interconnect with the same grid at a physically "proximate" location, should be viewed as no less physically co-located than a large load and a comparably-sized generation resource that interconnect with the same grid at a single point of interconnection, whether in front of or behind the meter.

We support the simultaneous study of system impacts from a Co-Located Load with its Co-Located Generation and the expeditious approval of the interconnection of both at a single point of interconnection or at two or more "proximate" points of interconnection, provided that the impacts on the transmission grid and other users of that transmission grid are addressed as set forth in Section III.B. of these Reply Comments.

the Commission and its Staff should now have a relatively complete record on "co-location" issues in PJM on which to formulate and propose guidance in response to the ANOPR regarding the range of acceptable transmission system protection provisions that counterparties could apply to co-location arrangements involving large loads and co-located generation resources located at the same point of interconnection or at "proximate" points of interconnection with the interstate transmission grid.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy points out that TO-only load studies miss cheaper transmission solutions visible only through a broader regional lens, as used in generator interconnection studies. A holistic approach reduces unnecessary overbuilding and keeps costs off non-large-load ratepayers.
quotes: load interconnections, unlike generator interconnection requests, are studied exclusively by each transmission owner and typically only include transmission solutions in that particular transmission owner's footprint, the study process often overlooks potentially less-expensive transmission solutions that would have been identified by looking at the system more holistically

letters.desc: Power-electronic large load control interactions with grid systems such as inverter-based resources are inherently location-specific, depending on grid strength and proximity to other systems. Studies and requirements must account for these interactions and regions must retain flexibility to protect their systems.
quotes: Require the large load interconnection study process to screen for, and assess, the potential for adverse oscillatory behaviors that may require physical (i.e., equipment upgrades) or operational measures to avoid, minimize and mitigate potentially adverse impacts upon the grid; and Allow interconnecting transmission owners to adopt general and locationally specific protection measures and equipment standards necessary to limit adverse oscillatory behavior from large loads and co-located loads.

there is substantial reason to expect that interconnection of large-load facilities dominated by power electronic loads requires specific attention to potential control interactions with other systems on the grid. The relevance of this issue and the necessary interconnection requirements and restrictions are inherently location-specific based on the strength of the grid and the proximity to potentially interacting systems.

The large load interconnection study process should assess the potential system impacts resulting from closed loop instability in the system and identify avoidance, minimization and mitigation measures that would reduce the risks of significant adverse impacts to the grid. Transmission owners should have the flexibility to identify locationally specific load facility oscillatory dampening characteristics that are necessary for system security and included in the development of the large load's interconnection facilities.

letters.org: Maine Office of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: Maine OPA supports measures to minimize adverse impacts on wholesale market prices and transmission rates. The filer emphasizes that large loads without matching generation can drive up energy and capacity prices, affecting all customers, and urges cautious implementation.
quotes: the Maine OPA urges the Commission to proceed with caution to ensure that any final rule protects existing ratepayers by requiring large loads to bear the full cost of necessary network upgrades, by respecting existing state jurisdiction over transactions that are fundamentally retail in nature, and by including provisions that minimize any adverse impacts on wholesale market prices and transmission rates from large load interconnection.

Absent the corresponding development of supply resources, the presence of new large loads will drive up market clearing prices for both energy and capacity in these wholesale markets, increasing retail prices for other customers.

The process for interconnecting large loads should not be a more accelerated process than that for generators. Doing so would likely trigger price increases for other customers if new loads are not matched with new generation.

Such mechanisms allow these new large loads to minimize their impact on both transmission rates and wholesale market prices, as well as to reduce the cost of interconnection and the ongoing cost of electricity to these customers.

letters.desc: The Market Monitor supports cost causation principles: new data center loads must bear the transmission and capacity costs they create rather than having those costs deferred or spread to existing customers through connect-and-manage or partial transmission cost calculations.
quotes: The Market Monitor agrees with PJM's points and thinks that PJM understates the negative outcomes of connect and manage. Ignoring the issues at the time of interconnection and imposing the actual costs as they are realized on other customers is not consistent with the stated purpose of the ANOPR.

All customers should be full NITS customers and pay their full share of transmission costs without calculations of asserted gross impacts, net impacts or other attempts to avoid paying for transmission service.

letters.desc: State jurisdiction is essential to prevent retail customers from subsidizing large-load customers or bearing unplanned risks. Rules must respect local conditions and priorities.
quotes: protection of state jurisdiction is essential to preventing retail customers from subsidizing large-load customers or bearing unplanned risks. FERC should ensure that any final rule respects the FPA's jurisdictional boundary and preserves New Mexico's sovereign authority to regulate retail service, resource decisions, and economic development consistent with state law and legislative priorities.

letters.desc: NREMC emphasizes that implementation must include regional flexibility to account for differences in queue structures, study methodologies, and status of current requests. RTOs, ISOs, and transmission providers need sufficient time to update procedures and staffing before new requirements take effect.
quotes: RTOs and ISOs, transmission providers, and load serving entities must have sufficient time to update their procedures, software, staffing, and coordination protocols before any new requirements take effect. Moreover, regional flexibility is necessary to account for differences in queue structures, study methodologies, and the status of current large-load interconnection requests.

letters.desc: NRG notes that miscalibrated cost allocation fails to signal to large loads where transmission investments would be cheapest, distorting siting decisions and leading to avoidable grid spending.
quotes: fail[s] to send a price signal for large load additions to locate in locations where the required transmission . . . investments for the large load would be lower.

letters.desc: Ohio FEA insists that new load interconnection must not compromise reliability of other customers and that speed must not come at the expense of safety and reliability, with utilities required to meet NERC standards and tariff requirements.
quotes: The interconnection of new large loads, however, must not come at the expense of reliability to other customers.
Speed is critical, but it must not come at the expense of safety and reliability.

letters.desc: Transmission planning rules should not bias the system toward unnecessary long-distance transmission when site-flexible alternatives exist. Planning must evaluate all options fairly, account for advanced nuclear deployment, and right-size transmission to actual demand.
quotes: FERC should revisit transmission planning rules, including those in Order No. 1920, to ensure they do not bias the system towards unnecessary transmission expansion when more efficient alternatives exist.

These technologies offer reliable, high-capacity-factor attributes without the need for costly, long-distance transmission projects. If the Commission's planning rules default towards identifying projects based on outdated location assumptions, they will overestimate transmission needs.

planning processes must evaluate alternatives on a level playing field and long-term scenarios must realistically account for advanced nuclear deployment rather than defaulting to intermittent resource characteristics.

letters.desc: OpenAI supports aligning cost responsibility with national infrastructure benefits and notes its commitment to invest in regional infrastructure upgrades that benefit surrounding communities.
quotes: we will invest a minimum of $175 million to make critical regional infrastructure upgrades (which benefit not just the hub but the surrounding community).
aligns cost responsibility with national infrastructure benefits

letters.desc: Paces argues that speculative, poorly sited load produces grid plans that do not match where load will actually be built. It recommends requiring parcel-level developability maps overlaid with bus-level headroom so planning and interconnection decisions reflect actual siting constraints.
quotes: manual study processes and speculative, project-by-project signals are producing slow interconnection queues and plans for load that will never be built, while a small set of constraints strands the load that actually can be built

Direct transmission providers that face material large-load growth to build parcel-level maps of developable large-load sites (zoning, setbacks, floodplains, water, ownership, etc.) and overlay them with bus-level withdrawal headroom.
sited at buses with positive headroom and nearby developable land
Permit slower timelines and clearer upgrade expectations for heavily constrained, non-power-ready locations.
the real operational risk is mis-located, speculative load plus manual-only study processes that cannot scale

letters.desc: JCA argue that large load customers are the but-for cause of new network expansion, monopolizing incremental capacity and providing no proportionate benefit to existing customers, which justifies assigning those costs entirely to the interconnecting customer.
quotes: the new large load customer may monopolize the incremental transmission capacity needed to serve them, meaning that the new pathway for electricity that ought to provide reliability and operational benefits is consumed by the large load customer's interconnection.

letters.desc: Each gigawatt served by CRE removes demand from the bulk system, reducing congestion, easing transmission strain, and shortening interconnection backlogs for other customers.
quotes: Every gigawatt of load served by a CRE system is one less gigawatt competing for scarce transmission capacity, straining aging infrastructure, or adding to the backlog of interconnection requests.

letters.desc: RSI notes that hybrid and flexible load configurations can reduce the need for network upgrades when their operational characteristics are properly modeled at interconnection, making them more suitable candidates for expedited federalized processes than load-only customers.
quotes: accelerating the interconnection of these load-and-FERC-jurisdictional-service configurations is warranted, given their outsized contribution to resource adequacy and limiting the impact on the broader transmission network.

letters.desc: Rewiring America advocates for defining asset proximity by measurable transmission relief capability rather than physical distance or bus count. This approach allows DER aggregations spanning multiple nodes to qualify when they can provide real, verifiable relief to the constrained area, avoiding exclusion of resources that contribute measurably to system benefit.
quotes: This lack of consensus creates a risk of adopting standards for asset proximity—such as a rigid bus-distance requirement—that exclude resources capable of providing real, verifiable relief to the same constrained portion of the grid.

what matters for system impact studies is the portion of the aggregated resource that can measurably relieve the specific constraint associated with the large load, even when the aggregation spans multiple nodes.

A resource should qualify as sufficiently proximate when it can provide timely, measurable, and locationally relevant relief to the transmission constraint created by the large load—regardless of its physical location, point of interconnection, or distance measured in buses.

letters.desc: Expedited large load queues must not impose delays or costs on generator interconnection customers already in standard queues, a key concern echoing Order No. 2023 protections.
quotes: Expedited study processes envisioned under this ANOPR should not cause delays, uncertainty, or allocation of new costs to generator interconnection customers already in queues.

letters.desc: SMA supports allocating interconnection and upgrade costs to the large load customer and not to general ratepayers, consistent with a proximate cost responsibility principle.
quotes: Cost responsibility should be ring-fenced so that general ratepayers are not burdened.

letters.desc: SEIA recommends that BYOG generators be electrically close to the associated load, either behind the same point of interconnection or at least in the same zone. This limits the network upgrades triggered and preserves open access for other queue participants.
quotes: The Commission should also not permit generation that agrees to be dispatchable to be expedited. As stated above, to maintain open access principles and not negatively impact generation projects that are already in the queue, BYOG arrangements must be electrically close, if not behind the same POI, then at least in the same zone.

letters.desc: SMECO warns that co-located hybrid large loads may dilute available generation supply and degrade resource adequacy, necessitating protective reliability frameworks.
quotes: SMECO appreciates the importance of ANOPR Principle 10 and urges the Commission to adopt a final rule to ensure that local reliability is not negatively impacted by hybrid/co-location arrangements, if such arrangements are to be permitted in the first instance at all.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group wants the final rule to define proximity by bus count rather than requiring the same point of interconnection, consistent with SPP's HILL rule allowing generators up to two substations away from the load's local delivery facilities.
quotes: the load also may be located within a specified number of buses to ensure that system impacts will be limited to a local area.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The HILL reform expedites study for generation electrically close to the load it serves, directly addressing the ANOPR's proximate-generation principle through a region-specific mechanism.
quotes: The HILL reform provides a 90-day expedited review process for generation projects in close electrical proximity to the load they are meant to serve.

letters.desc: Terraflux proposes that near-located means within three busbar substations, distinguishing it from co-located which means the same busbar substation.
quotes: We agree with the third principle's assertion that both co-located and near-located load plus generation facilities should be studied together as hybrid facilities, rather than forced to be studied as one separate load interconnection request and one separate generation interconnection request. We propose that 'near-located' means within three busbar substations of each other, while 'co-located' means within the same busbar substation.

letters.desc: Pew endorses a performance-based, location-aware standard for VPP eligibility: what matters is that the resource mitigates constraints in the same constrained transmission pocket, not whether it sits inside or outside the facility fence line. Aggregated DERs in close electrical proximity should qualify as adjacent supply.
quotes: [W]hat matters is equivalent, verifiable performance in mitigating constraints within the same constrained transmission pocket or local grid area, not whether the asset is physically inside or outside the facility fence line.
Aggregated DERs, again, should be eligible as 'adjacent supply' in this example, because they are as able to reduce the new large load's transmission system impacts as utility-scale resources.

letters.desc: TBA calls for consistent application of non-firm assumptions across all study types so that planning outcomes reflect actual load behavior rather than conservative firm-load assumptions.
quotes: non-firm loads must be modeled in interconnection, transmission service, and planning studies consistent with their curtailment rights

letters.desc: Tract supports crediting load customers for network upgrade costs proportional to actual use by other networked customers, with no fixed expiration on the credit period.
quotes: To the extent any network upgrades are assigned through interconnection studies to load or hybrid facilities, such costs should be offset through a crediting mechanism based on the actual usage of those upgrades by other networked customers.

letters.desc: The filer asks FERC to allow flexibility commitments to be met by resources physically or electrically adjacent to the load, and cites SPP's substation-distance presumption as a useful model for clear pairing rules.
quotes: The Commission should also ensure that load commitments to flexibility can be met by resources physically and/or electrically adjacent to load.

SPP’s recent High Impact Large Load proposal would enable expedited interconnection for load paired with generation, if the resources are within two substations of one another, or one substation if the transmission facility between them is 765kV.

letters.desc: The filers ask FERC to assess how clustering of large loads within a single region affects transmission congestion and generation adequacy, framing geographic concentration as a distinct planning problem beyond individual interconnection review.
quotes: Cumulative impacts of multiple large facilities locating within a single region, including effects on transmission congestion, local generation adequacy, and resource adequacy planning.

letters.org: Utility Intervention Unit, New York State Department of Stat
letters.desc: The UIU urges that when a generator exits the market to serve a large load behind the meter, an RMR-type forward study must confirm no resource adequacy shortfall results. Existing load customers must not absorb higher capacity costs from that market exit.
quotes: In no instance should existing load customers be on the hook for increased capacity costs (this includes the cost of RMR-style contracts) because a generator has decided to exit the market to serve a large load BTM.

letters.desc: Verrus cites the SPP HILLGA approach of studying loads together with electrically proximate generation as a model FERC should adopt nationwide, because the integrated approach can identify co-location opportunities that reduce upgrade needs and speed interconnection.
quotes: Southwest Power Pool's ("SPP") recent High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment ("HILLGA") proposal recognizes that integrating the study of load with electrically proximate generation/resources is more efficient than standalone regulation.

letters.desc: The VSCC contends that keeping load interconnection at the state level best preserves integrated resource planning, where load forecasting and supply adequacy are planned together. Federal takeover would disrupt this in vertically integrated states.
quotes: The shared authority the VSCC proposes would best address resource adequacy concerns, as it would keep load and supply planning together at the state level. This is particularly important in vertically integrated states with robust integrated resource planning regimes.

letters.desc: Vistra supports measuring a co-located facility's transmission service and network upgrade obligations based on net injections and withdrawals, not gross load, as required by Federal Power Act cost causation principles.
quotes: Cost causation principles require that the parties to such an arrangement fund any necessary network upgrades, and the transmission service that facilitates these arrangements be determined by actual use of the transmission system based on their net load.
transmission providers should serve, and charge, co-located facilities based on their actual use of the transmission system, i.e., based on their net—not gross—injections and withdrawals.

letters.desc: The filers argue supporting capacity need not be physically co-located but can be distributed across the area where the load affects constraints, so long as the operator can control it. They ask that electrically proximate or adjacent assets count in study prioritization and incentives, and that such capacity be geographically transferable via wholesale capacity credits.
quotes: The ANOPR Seventh Principle4 should include incremental Distributed Capacity in the form of load flexibility, storage, and/or generation capacity whose location can address capacity and transmission constraints projected to be caused by the new large loads, even if such capacity is located on the distribution system.

These comments endorse the above principles while expanding on them to ensure that “electrically proximate” or “adjacent” grid assets—assets that can mitigate the constraints imposed by new loads where those constraints actually occur—are also considered in study prioritization, netted against load withdrawals for study purposes, and included in speed-to-power incentive structures.

new capacity supporting large loads need not be physically co-located at the facility, but can be distributed across the geographic area within which the new load will impact system constraints, provided that the system operator has the requisite level of control to integrate the facility into operations and system planning.

capacity—including batteries, generation, and demand response (DR)—should be geographically transferable in the form of capacity credits as defined by the wholesale market, or within the TOs system planning paradigm.

letters.desc: Off-site distributed resources located within the constrained transmission area or local grid provide equivalent network benefits to co-located assets and should receive equivalent treatment in studies and interconnection. Appropriateness is determined by the resource's ability to mitigate the load's impacts, not its physical fence-line location.
quotes: that large loads . . . that enter into arrangements with another appropriately located load aggregation to provide . . . curtailment be considered when exploring expedited interconnection processes that respect existing queue positions.

can be distributed across the geographic area within which the new load will impact system constraints, provided that the system operator has the requisite level of control to integrate the facility into operations and system planning.
[s]uch resources may share a point of interconnection or be in close (electrical) proximity to one another . . . and may warrant accelerated treatment to connect to the grid
offset their load through the addition of timely, local, and adequate capacity resources

what matters is equivalent, verifiable performance in mitigating constraints within the same constrained transmission pocket or local grid area, not whether the asset is physically inside or outside the facility fence line.
appropriately located off-site resources provide network benefits on par with those provided by on-site resources, and should be studied and interconnected with equivalent priority.

such adjacent flexibility refers to the ability to coordinate with nearby or aggregated resources (e.g., a local VPP) via a software interface, so that the net effect reduces withdrawals on constrained parts of the grid.

[Capacity] solutions need not originate at the site of a new large load but could be incremental flexibility that is contracted by that large load and that is located such that it counteracts the impacts of the new large load.

letters.org: Wisconsin Electric Power CompanyWisconsin Public Service Corporation
letters.desc: WEC asks the Commission to recognize that proximity to working processes matters: regions like Wisconsin with functioning state and RTO frameworks should be exempted or allowed to vary from any national rule under an independent-entity variation standard.
quotes: any rulemaking pursuant to the ANOPR should be limited and apply only to regions that do not have similarly strong processes in place.

the Commission should honor established processes that are working well and should not apply federal rules to regions where there are existing or proposed processes or tariffs, such as in Wisconsin.  At a minimum, the Commission should apply the "independent entity variation" standard to load interconnection rules, as it does the generator interconnection rules.

letters.desc: ECA cautions that directly singling out large load-driven regional transmission costs may seem to improve cost causation alignment but could undermine more efficient multi-value regional planning that benefits all consumers over the long term. Targeted assignment and broader regional approaches both have real tradeoffs that policymakers must weigh carefully.
quotes: singling out large load-driven regional transmission costs may appear to improve alignment with the cost causation principle in the near term, but could undermine more efficient, multi-value regional planning that produces broader long-term benefits for consumers.

letters.desc: APS expresses concern that without clear NERC standards for hybrid facilities, the burden of managing frequency deviations caused by load-generation mismatches will fall to the host utility.
quotes: the burden would fall to the host utility to manage frequency deviations caused by mismatches.

letters.desc: LS Power, citing EPSA, opposes ANOPR Principle 10's premise that moving existing generation behind the meter to serve data center load constitutes a partial suspension. Any reliability review should be limited to safe and reliable interconnection, not broad resource adequacy analysis.
quotes: LS Power does not support this principle and supports the EPSA position on this principle.

EPSA rejects the underlying premise that existing generation that is moved behind the meter to serve data center load is akin to a partial suspension or otherwise warrants RMR/SSR type analysis for deactivating resources.

letters.desc: Maven contends that Constellation's reliability argument rests on a footnote assertion that 'mechanisms similar to those used in surplus or hybrid interconnection would be in place,' without a protection design basis, clearing-time analysis, or failure-mode study. The Commission cannot set a just and reasonable rate on an undemonstrated promise.
quotes: That footnote is doing the structural work of the entire reliability argument. It is not a protection design. It is not a clearing-time analysis. It is not a failure-mode study. It is a promise—and the Commission does not set just and reasonable rates on promises.

letters.desc: FERC rules on large load interconnection must follow close consultation with states and preserve state authority over siting, permitting, and taxation. Federal preemption of state jurisdiction requires safeguards and meaningful state participation in stakeholder discussions.
quotes: This new proposed rule would bring under federal jurisdiction an issue that is currently handled by the states and has been for decades. While NCSL understands the need for enhanced oversight over how large loads obtain power any such regulatory decisions by FERC should only come after close, careful and deliberate consultation with states early and often throughout the process of rule development to ensure individual and small rate payers are protected.

Include state policy makers in all stakeholder discussions regarding data center placement and energy usage and refrain from pre-empting states on siting, permitting, taxation and other regulatory issues relating to the construction and operation of data centers.

letters.org: Natural Resource Defense CouncilSustainable FERC ProjectClean Air Task Force ,Coalition for Affordable Utility Services and Energy Efficie ,EARTHJUSTICE ,ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENSE FUND ,MONTANA ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION CENTER ,Sierra Club ,Southern Environmental Law Center ,
letters.desc: The filers oppose Principle 10 because allowing an existing generator to suspend service to the broader market to serve one data center customer removes capacity already paid for by existing ratepayers and increases their resource adequacy costs and blackout risk.
quotes: PIOs do not believe that the Commission should adopt Principle 10. Many regions of the country are currently experiencing resource adequacy or reliability challenges. Generation that has been on the system and serving existing load should not be allowed to be essentially removed from the grid to serve a single customer.

the suspension of existing generation to serve new large loads is inconsistent with cost-causation principles and unjust and unreasonable because this practice shifts costs associated with maintaining resource adequacy onto other consumers, as well as increasing reliability risks for existing ratepayers.

letters.org: North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff
letters.desc: Any final rule should not constrain state authority over the siting of transmission or over generation facilities serving retail customers.
quotes: any final rule should place no constraints, express or implied, on the authority of states to set the terms and rates for retail customers over generation facilities, or over the siting of transmission.

letters.desc: AES notes the ANOPR's hybrid facility definition may not capture the range of actual configurations, from separately metered shared interconnection points to fully islanded generation, and asks FERC to seek further comment before locking in a definition.
quotes: AES believes that the Commission should distinguish between co-location of loads with new versus existing generation, as the impacts to existing customers will differ.

letters.desc: APGA highlights the proximate relationship between large electric loads and the gas transmission system: gas-fired data centers draw from the same interstate pipelines that public utilities depend on. Without coordination, pipeline capacity strain could impair public gas systems' ability to meet their obligation to serve, and firm transportation rights must be preserved.
quotes: they may impact the reliability of the natural gas transmission system, creating downstream impacts on APGA members' ability to reliably and affordably serve their communities and customers.
Any policy changes must preserve public gas utilities' flexibility in exercising their firm transportation rights and protect their ability to serve residential and commercial customers.
Without thoughtful planning and coordination, increased demand on pipelines could strain existing capacity and jeopardize the ability of public gas systems to meet their core obligation to serve.

letters.desc: The filer notes that large loads are highly elastic and can relocate or self-supply, making full upgrade cost assignment counterproductive. This frames the proximate-load question in terms of economic efficiency rather than geography.
quotes: Because large loads are highly elastic and can relocate or self-supply, assigning them full upgrade costs encourages inefficient grid defection.

letters.desc: The filer explains that Ireland requires dispatchable generation to be on-site or proximate for large data centres, while permitting remote renewable generation for the annual energy target. This distinction illustrates how proximity rules can be calibrated to different reliability and decarbonisation objectives.
quotes: CRU does not allow a data centre to meet its capacity obligation using remote generation elsewhere in Ireland. However, it does allow remote renewable generation to count toward the 80% renewable requirement.
